videos.title: Would A Great White Survive Every Prehistoric Ocean?
chapters: Is the great white really the king of the ocean?
Ordovician (450 million years ago): giant orthocones
Devonian (370 million years ago): great white vs Dunkleosteus
Carboniferous (300 million years ago): Stethacanthus and Helicoprion
Triassic (250 million years ago): giant ichthyosaurs
Jurassic (160 million years ago): Liopleurodon and the pliosaurs
Cretaceous (80 million years ago): Tylosaurus, the mosasaur
Miocene (15 million years ago): Megalodon and Livyatan
Pliocene (5 million years ago): the end of the megalodon
Modern ocean: orcas vs great whites
videos.title_formula: Would A [Familiar Apex Animal] Survive Every Prehistoric Ocean?  (yes/no question + 'every' tournament; clone of Fossil's 'Would Orcas Dominate Every Prehistoric Ocean?' 3.8M)
videos.thumbnail: Black bg, engraving great white with gold crown left, 4 prehistoric monsters (orthocone, Dunkleosteus, mosasaur, megalodon) stacked right; text 'Still King?' white + red 'King?'. Near copy of Fossil's 'New King?' orca thumbnail.
videos.visual_style: Different art style: outlined cartoon creatures (dark outline, cel shading), teal water with god rays, beige/green flat landscapes, map cards; kinetic word captions with one orange/red emphasised word ('fly out of the WATER.'); era title cards ('500 MILLION YEARS AGO / CAMBRIAN PERIOD'); rotating 'DT' time-dial transitions; crown/check/skull scoreboard; vertical depth gauge each era.
